packets.title: composite_scene — the single compositing pipeline shared by render() and render_to_pixels()
packets.responsibility: THE single compositing pipeline (a documented invariant: all rendering logic goes here, never duplicated into render()/render_to_pixels()). Fast path (no blend/matte/effects/mask/folder anywhere in the scene): one Scene, paint every layer's items directly, one render_to_texture call. Slow path: ping-pong accumulator cleared TRANSPARENT (a 2026-08-31 fix — clearing opaque previously hid the canvas background under any non-default blend-mode layer), canvas-background painted into its own isolated texture BEFORE the main loop so an Effect/adjustment layer's backdrop read can never include it, then per-layer: skip matte-source/folder-child layers, effect/adjustment layers grade the running accumulator in place, folder layers recursively flatten just their children into a separate accumulator pair (nested folders unsupported v1 — a folder-shaped child is deliberately left OUT of the skip-set so it still renders independently rather than silently vanishing), vector masks combine (Add union, Subtract/Intersect chained) reusing the matte pipeline's own alpha-multiply math, then matte, then blend-mode composite into the outer accumulator.
packets.writer: sole writer of the compositing algorithm; called by exactly render() and render_to_pixels() (the only two callers)
packets.public_api: private (not pub, not wasm_bindgen) — internal to VelloEngine's plain impl block

packets.title: Retained vector-geometry store — Paper _changed hook, motion affine mirror, ref registry
packets.responsibility: The retained-geometry mechanism in full: (1) installGeometryHook probes Paper.js's undocumented ChangeFlag bits at runtime (geometry-only mask = geometry bits minus style bits, measured not hardcoded) and monkey-patches BOTH Path.prototype._changed and Item.prototype._changed (Path has its own — Paper's class system captures `base` by reference, so patching Item alone misses Path entirely, verified empirically) to null an item's __engineSrcDict stamp on any geometry mutation and flag its parent layer `_smGeomDirty`; (2) affineFromMotion/affineMul/motionChainUniform mirror motion.js's transformSegments EXACTLY (scale in pivot-local frame, rotate around pivot, translate last) so an animated shape can still use its registered path — motionChainUniform gates this to uniform-scale-only chains (non-uniform would need an elliptical pen the engine's affine-stroke can't express, so those fall back to inline); (3) existingPathRef/pathRefFor/flushRetiredPaths are the WeakMap-keyed register/lookup/retire lifecycle, capped at _registerCap=250000 as a hard backstop against a future layer-kind that synthesizes fresh dicts per call (symbolId/montageId/lfsGroup all do this and must never be registered from).

packets.title: Engine create/enable/disable/resize lifecycle and failure handling

packets.title: fill_find — planar-graph face tracing for the paint-bucket tool
packets.responsibility: A single cohesive pipeline behind one export, decomposing into 4 sequential internal stages never independently invoked: (a) generic 2D polyline/curve geometry primitives; (b) crossing detection and planar-graph construction from raw wall polylines, with spur-pruning and duplicate-edge collapsing; (c) exhaustive graph face-tracing via sharpest-relative-turn selection at each directed half-edge; (d) result reconstruction — picks the smallest-area containing face and re-samples it from the exact bezier curves.
packets.writer: fill_find is the sole owner of every intermediate structure it builds per call; one exception — std::env::var("FILL_DEBUG") reads ambient process environment state controlling only logging, not the return value
packets.public_api: fill_find(input_json: &str) -> Result<String, JsValue> — #[wasm_bindgen]; all input/output types are private, JSON-string-in/JSON-string-out only
consumers: src/js/tools.js:3494-3507 (fillVectorFindWasm, builds the {openWalls,closedWalls,gapThr,click,crossings} shape and branches on res.kind: notFound/closedWall/traced)
packets.oracle: 1 #[cfg(test)] test (fill.rs:1011-1036, mod circle_lens_tests): two_crossing_circles_lens_is_traced feeds a literal captured payload reproducing GitHub feedback #116, asserts the result is 'traced' and the returned bounding box exactly matches the known lens region within 1.0px — a regression oracle for a specific trace_loop arrival-direction fix. No external geometry-wasm/tests/*.rs coverage found.
packets.notes: struct PathSampler here (95-132) is a from-scratch mirror of tweenmatch.rs's PathSampler idiom, explicitly acknowledged in this file's own comment; struct Vec2 (58-74) reimplements basic 2D vector math instead of using vello::kurbo::Point/Vec2, which the crate already depends on and which tweenmatch.rs imports directly. eprintln! debug-logging (gated only by the FILL_DEBUG env-var runtime check, not #[cfg(...)]) is compiled into the binary unconditionally. A final-result self-intersection recheck can flip a would-be Traced result to NotFound purely from floating-point differences between the coarse candidate-selection tolerance and the exact final resample.

packets.title: track_points / track_grid — pyramidal Lucas-Kanade optical-flow tracking
packets.responsibility: A single algorithm — pyramidal Lucas-Kanade optical-flow point tracking between two luminance images — exposed at three strictly-nested layers, not independent responsibilities: the numerical core (track_level and pyramid-building helpers), the 'track an arbitrary list of points' batch entry that the wasm export wraps, and the 'track a regular grid, package as a motion field' convenience entry that interp.rs's dense image-warping consumes. track_level -> track_points_impl -> track_grid is a strict call chain.
packets.writer: track_points_impl is the sole producer of TrackOut; track_grid is the sole producer of GridFlow, and — because TrackOut's points/ok fields are private — also the only code able to read them from outside track_points_impl itself
packets.public_api: track_points(input_json: &str) -> Result<String,JsValue> — #[wasm_bindgen] (only this is re-exported from lib.rs; track_points_impl/track_grid/GridFlow/TrackIn/TrackOut are pub but crate-internal-reachability only)
consumers: src/js/tracker.js:128 (trackLayer, per-frame in a loop; a point returning ok:false aborts the rest of the tracked range) — real, live caller

geometry-wasm/src/interp.rs:27,193 (the ONLY Rust consumer, via track_grid/GridFlow — note the dependency direction: track.rs has zero outbound internal dependencies, interp.rs depends on it, not the reverse)

packets.notes: Inconsistent field-visibility pattern: TrackOut is pub but 2 of its 3 fields are private, while the sibling GridFlow makes all 7 fields pub — no other module needs TrackOut's fields directly, so this is asymmetric by accident of usage rather than by clear design intent. Validation-check asymmetry: the wasm entry point track_points bounds-checks prev/next length against width*height, but neither track_points_impl nor track_grid (which interp.rs calls directly) performs the equivalent check themselves — today's only direct caller happens to always supply correctly-sized buffers. No duplication found with tweenmatch.rs — the two solve unrelated numerical problems (dense pixel-flow vs. discrete stroke assignment) with no shared types.

cross_cutting_notes: engine-bridge.js is consumed by 68 other JS files (repo-wide grep of `SMEngineBridge\.` call sites) — by a wide margin the single most widely-depended-on file found in this census. Heaviest consumers by call-site count: motion.js (83), select-bridge.js (70), timeline.js (78), tools.js (41), draw-bridge.js (28), fill-bridge.js (20), native-video-bridge.js (20), rig-bridge.js (22), eraser-bridge.js (18), image-mesh-bridge.js (16). Any extraction or refactor of this file has by far the largest blast radius of anything in the C03 scope.

Two independent VelloEngine instances can coexist at runtime — the main one (engine-bridge.js) and a second, fully independent one created by src/js/second-viewer.js (out of bounded scope) for its own duplicate-viewer canvas. Each instance owns its own complete copy of every GPU texture/pipeline cluster described in C03.gpu-engine-core.vello-engine-state, and each JS-side resource store (bounded image budget, retained-path store) is scoped to engine-bridge.js's own module closure — second-viewer.js is not confirmed to share either budget. Opening a second viewer likely doubles GPU memory footprint with no unified budget coordinating the two.

src/js/geometry-wasm-loader.js (out of bounded scope, read for context) is the single authoritative place every geometry-wasm wasm-bindgen export is bound onto window.GeometryWasm.*. It was used throughout this census to determine ground truth for which Rust exports are actually reachable from JS at all, and should be included in the same extraction unit as (or explicitly declared as a dependency of) engine-bridge.js's engine-lifecycle packet if engine-bridge.js is ever split.

A recurring 'exported to wasm-bindgen (or to a public JS object) but never called from anywhere live' pattern was independently confirmed, by direct repo-wide grep rather than assumption, at least 9 times across this census: geometry-wasm hit.rs::hit_test (self-documented by its own author), tween.rs::interp_stroke (self-documented, with an explicit do-not-wire-in-yet warning), timeline.rs::resolve_symbol_frame and ::effective_frame_index (NOT self-documented — a newly-surfaced duplicate-implementation risk against app.js's own native-JS equivalents), interp.rs::FlowField::magnitude() (narrower — the surrounding compute_flow/interpolate_at module IS live), lib.rs::boolean_op (only boolean_op_multi is ever called), engine.rs's entire Phase-C3 selection API (select_at/clear_selection/get_selection/selection_bounds/gizmo_handles/scale_selection/rotate_selection — select_at is reached only from Rust-internal code, never from JS), and engine-bridge.js's preview-render-scale calibration API (getPreviewRenderScale/getPreviewCalibStatus/setPreviewRenderScale/forcePreviewCalibration) and render-manager.js's setBudgetBytes-equivalent in playback-cache.js. Any completeness sweep (C08) or extraction plan should treat 'is this export actually live' as a question to re-verify per item, not assume from a function's mere existence.

Structural type duplication across the geometry-wasm crate, found independently while reading three separate files: SegIn is defined identically in engine.rs, tween.rs, AND tweenmatch.rs (3 independent Rust struct definitions of the same wire shape); SegOut is defined identically in fill.rs, tween.rs, tweenmatch.rs, AND shapes.rs (4 independent definitions). None of these share a common type despite being byte-identical in shape.

The PathSampler idiom (arc-length-parameterized point/tangent sampling of a BezPath) is independently re-implemented, not shared, in both tweenmatch.rs and fill.rs — fill.rs's own comment explicitly acknowledges mirroring tweenmatch.rs's version rather than reusing it.

A cross-file duplication with a REAL semantic divergence, not just cosmetic repetition: the `hasRealStroke` guard concept appears as near-identical inline ternaries independently in color-manager.js (2 sites) and motion.js (2 sites) using `sd.hasRealStroke !== undefined ? sd.hasRealStroke : !!sd.strokeColor`, but shapes-panel.js's independently-written named helper uses `!== false` instead of `!== undefined` in its equivalent check — a genuine behavioral difference between 'the same' guard depending on which file's copy runs.

render-manager.js and color-manager.js both have zero automated test coverage AND are absent from .c8rc.json's coverage-gate `include` allowlist — i.e. structurally exempted from the enforced coverage gate, not merely untested by omission. playback-cache.js has exactly one test covering one specific optimization (canvas-backing-store reuse) and no coverage of any of its other 11 public methods. shader-effects-library.js has no JS-level test at all, but does have two genuine, currently-passing Rust integration tests (shader_library_validation.rs, effect_layer_overlay_repro.rs) that load and validate its raw content via a Node subprocess — its ONLY real regression coverage lives on the Rust side of the boundary, not the JS side.

None of tweenmatch.rs, fill.rs, or track.rs's wasm-exported functions are called from engine-bridge.js — a premise this census initially assumed and then corrected mid-investigation. The real call sites are src/js/tweens.js (auto_match, resample_stroke, align_pair), src/js/tools.js (fill_find, and separately boolean_op_multi from lib.rs), and src/js/tracker.js (track_points), all wired through geometry-wasm-loader.js. engine-bridge.js's only geometry-wasm touchpoints are the readiness check and create_engine itself.

known_defects.summary: FlowField::magnitude() is a #[wasm_bindgen]-exported method with zero callers anywhere in the repo, Rust or JS (confirmed by grep). The surrounding module (compute_flow/interpolate_at) is genuinely live via native-video-bridge.js; this one method specifically is not.

hit_test (the #[wasm_bindgen] JSON-string wrapper) has zero JS callers anywhere in src/js, confirmed independently of — and matching — the file's own 2026-07-13 self-documented claim. Only the internal hit_test_scene is load-bearing, via engine.rs's select_at.

resolve_symbol_frame and effective_frame_index are fully-ported, wasm-exported equivalents of app.js's resolveSymbolFrameIdx/getEffectiveStrokes, but have zero JS callers — the app's live logic runs entirely through the independently-maintained native-JS originals instead. Unlike hit.rs/tween.rs, this is NOT self-documented in the file's own comments, making it a real drift risk: a future bug fix to the JS originals will not propagate here.

interp_stroke is confirmed dead from JS (zero callers). Self-documented by the file's own header as an intentionally-unwired, earlier-vintage port that has fallen behind the current JS reference (missing similarity-transform/rotation-scale blending that tweenmatch.rs already computes internally) — the header explicitly warns not to wire it in without first porting that gap.

boolean_op (singular, non-multi variant) has no direct JS call site anywhere in the repo — only boolean_op_multi is ever called (tools.js:5854), reached exclusively through its multi-operand fold wrapper.

The entire Phase-C3 selection wasm-bindgen API (select_at, clear_selection, get_selection, selection_bounds, gizmo_handles, scale_selection, rotate_selection) has zero callers anywhere in src/js (confirmed by repo-wide grep). select_at is reached only internally, from no confirmed caller either — this whole surface appears to be unwired future-phase scaffolding.

The preview-render-scale calibration public API (getPreviewRenderScale, getPreviewCalibStatus, setPreviewRenderScale, forcePreviewCalibration) has zero callers anywhere in src/js — ui.js's only SMEngineBridge call is an unrelated renderNow(). The calibration mechanism itself IS live (it self-triggers via recordCalibSample during normal rendering), but none of its introspection/override API is ever exercised from outside the module.
known_defects.severity: dead code (public API only; internal mechanism is live)

known_defects.summary: setBudgetBytes has zero callers anywhere in the repo despite being a public setter with real, correct clamping logic (Math.max(1,Math.floor(n))) — the 256MB budget is permanently hardcoded in practice.

shapes-panel.js's own hasRealStroke(sd) helper uses `!!sd.isVectorBrush || (!!sd.strokeColor && sd.hasRealStroke !== false)`, while the equivalent inline guard duplicated independently in color-manager.js (2 sites) and motion.js (2 sites) uses `sd.hasRealStroke !== undefined ? sd.hasRealStroke : !!sd.strokeColor` — a real semantic divergence (`!== false` vs. `!== undefined`) between five independent implementations of what is intended to be the same check, not merely cosmetic duplication.
known_defects.severity: correctness risk (semantic divergence across duplicated logic)

known_defects.summary: lib.rs's `mod strokemodeler;` declaration has no matching `pub use` re-export, unlike every other one of the crate's 11 modules — harmless today (wasm-bindgen scans the whole crate regardless, and nothing in Rust references crate::StrokeModeler), but an inconsistency in the module-declaration pattern that could confuse a future Rust-side consumer expecting the same convention.
known_defects.severity: informational (pattern inconsistency, not a runtime gap)
